title: Screens and Game States
summary: A finished game has a title screen, the game itself, a pause menu, a game-over screen and transitions between them. This lesson organises a game into screens - first with an enum and a switch, then with screen objects on a stack - and fades smoothly from one to the next.

cards.q: What makes a set of screens a state machine?
cards.a: There is always exactly one current screen, and events move the game from one screen to another.

cards.q: Why is a stack useful for a pause menu?
cards.a: The game stays below the menu, frozen and still drawn, and popping the menu returns to it exactly as it was.

cards.q: Why should scenes request stack changes instead of changing the stack directly?
cards.a: Popping the scene whose update is running would destroy it while its code is still executing.
